mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and corporate earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 4% signals a supply-side shock in a tight labor market, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher pricing power and profit margins.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 5%) combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 flat or falling YoY) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a softening economic cycle and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL of more than 0.5% (after two months of prior increases) signals a sudden drop in inflation expectations, which typically coincides with a loosening of monetary policy and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as risk premia compress.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% in one month after two months of increases
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate simultaneously falls below 3.5% signals an exceptionally tight labor market, which historically precedes above-average S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to wage inflation and margin expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 8% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which is historically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to correlated construction and materials sector outperformance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
